tasks.short: Review sustainability proposals and revise policies with stakeholders before approval.

steps.what: Gather the proposal, current policy, and supporting evidence.
Compare proposed wording against evidence, commitments, and policy requirements.

loop.input: Proposal passages and a versioned pack of approved evidence and requirements.
loop.output: Passage-level issues, supporting citations, and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Verify cited passages exist; specialist checks interpretations and missing obligations.
loop.stop: One comparison and one correction pass per section; unresolved issues go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules detect missing fields, but cannot reliably interpret qualified commitments in prose.

steps.what: Discuss feasibility and trade-offs with operational, procurement, finance, and legal stakeholders.
Revise policy wording and document the reasons for changes.

loop.input: Current policy, agreed revisions, approved terminology, and policy template.
loop.output: Tracked policy revisions and a change log.
loop.check: Check every change against a recorded decision; specialist verifies obligations and qualifications.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported commitments remain flagged for manual drafting.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle structure, but revisions require coherent wording across related clauses.

steps.what: Approve the revised policy and its organizational commitments.
Publish the approved version and notify affected policy owners.

tasks.design: A review-pack generator gathers versioned evidence from the {DOCS}; bounded comparison and drafting loops produce cited issues and tracked revisions. Stakeholders resolve trade-offs, and the sustainability sponsor approves commitments through the {WORKFLOW}. Approval triggers publication in the {DOCS} and notifications through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, and policy interpretation required expertise. Templates could standardize layout but could not resolve ambiguous commitments.
tasks.enabler_now: Faster code assembly makes evidence indexing and version checks cheaper. Bounded reading and drafting loops can work from a controlled source pack.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting objectives, uncertain evidence, and national rules still require specialist and legal judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize when an attractive commitment cannot be delivered, and negotiate wording that people will follow.

ambition.what: Quarterly review of sustainability commitments against new operational evidence.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling documents and more time resolving policy trade-offs. They gain responsibility for recommending review priorities; approval rights stay with the sponsor.

reach.task: Turn approved sustainability policies into practical operating instructions.
reach.learn: Controlled language, document architecture, and testing instructions with operational readers.

evidence.claim: Policy review typically combines document comparison, stakeholder discussion, drafting, and approval.
Versioned retrieval and bounded drafting can reduce preparation work while leaving policy decisions human.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The document-heavy and judgement-heavy priors fit this decomposition; stakeholder discussion remains substantial.
A named sponsor approves commitments, and approved evidence can be versioned.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and may overlap.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. National rules determine any employee consultation requirements.
unknowns: Who can approve policy changes and which changes require legal review?
Which reporting and environmental obligations apply to this organization?
Are policy versions, evidence permissions, and approval histories reliable?
Does the policy affect employee data or monitoring, requiring consultation under national rules?
research_questions: Can comparison quality be demonstrated on policies containing exceptions and qualified commitments?
Which existing document approval features cover publication and version control?
new_work: Review proposed interpretations and policy wording.
Maintain the approved evidence set and requirement register.
Handle conflicting stakeholder decisions and unsupported commitments.
Check permissions, publication rules, and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Review and revise sustainability proposals or policies.

tasks.short: Research sustainability rules, technical options and market developments, then explain their organizational implications.

steps.what: Define the research question, organizational scope and deadline.
Retrieve regulatory, technical and market sources from {GOV_PORTAL} and research portals {OTHER}.
Read sources and compare requirements, evidence quality and competing interpretations.

loop.input: Retrieved source text, research question and required evidence fields.
loop.output: Evidence table with quotations, source locations, dates and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Check quoted passages against stored sources; flag unsupported statements and ambiguous legal status.
loop.stop: One extraction pass and one repair pass per source, capped at 20 sources; unresolved items return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Different document structures and narrative qualifications prevent reliable extraction through fixed fields alone.

steps.what: Discuss applicability, operational consequences and unresolved interpretations with responsible colleagues.
Write a briefing with recommendations, evidence links and remaining uncertainties.

loop.input: Reviewed evidence table, implication assessment and briefing template.
loop.output: Briefing draft separating source facts, specialist interpretations and proposed actions.
loop.check: Require source references for factual claims; compare recommendations with the implication assessment.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at two model calls; failed checks fall back to the template.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template supplies structure, but explaining varied implications requires narrative synthesis.

steps.what: Approve and circulate the briefing to responsible teams.

tasks.design: Start with an uploaded source pack and a research register in {DOCS}; scheduled retrieval on {DATA_PLATFORM} adds permitted sources from {GOV_PORTAL}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops create cited briefings, while {WORKFLOW} routes approval and sends release notifications through {EMAIL}. Applicability discussions stay with the specialist and responsible colleagues.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources vary in format, status and terminology. Retrieval could already be automated, but interpretation and briefing preparation needed substantial manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can shorten implementation of retrieval, provenance checks and templates. Bounded text processing can prepare evidence tables without taking responsibility for legal interpretation.
tasks.still_hard: Determining applicability, resolving conflicting sources and accessing licensed technical material remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist connects evidence to actual operations and distinguishes a binding obligation from guidance or a market signal.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on whether new sustainability developments require an operational response.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less source collection and briefing assembly, with more time for applicability discussions. Decision rights remain unchanged unless management delegates authority to prioritize the response backlog.

reach.task: Assess demand for a proposed sustainable offering.
reach.learn: Learn sampling, market segmentation and how to distinguish stated preferences from purchasing behavior.

evidence.claim: Source retrieval and briefing assembly are plausible automation targets; applicability judgment remains human.
The digest reports narrowed CSRD thresholds; organizational applicability must be established before recommending reporting work.
A documented report failure involving invented references supports source checks before releasing generated research.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured results.
The starter accepts uploaded documents without requiring company-wide integrations.
The estimate covers a small approved source list and one briefing format.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the actual deployment; national rules vary.
The high automation prior is tempered by the time needed for applicability judgment.
unknowns: Which jurisdictions, sectors and legal entities the organization covers.
Which sources permit automated retrieval and reuse.
Who approves briefings and when legal counsel must review interpretations.
Whether internal research material contains personal or confidential data.
research_questions: Which source types produce the most extraction errors?
Can reviewers trace each briefing claim to an exact source passage?
How much collection time remains after source access restrictions are applied?
new_work: Maintain the approved source register and retrieval permissions.
Review missing passages, conflicting interpretations and outdated sources.
Maintain briefing templates and extraction checks.
Track approved response actions and unresolved questions.
tasks.statement: Research or review regulatory, technical, or market issues related to sustainability.

tasks.short: Investigate suspected environmental policy violations and establish findings and corrective actions.

steps.what: Register a reported concern and assign an investigation owner.
Retrieve waste movements, supplier records and relevant operating records.
Inspect the site and document conditions, quantities and physical evidence.
Interview relevant staff about what happened and why.
Compare evidence against policy requirements and identify contradictions or gaps.

loop.input: Case evidence and approved policy passages.
loop.output: Evidence-to-policy table with contradictions, missing evidence and possible breaches.
loop.check: Verify every reference; specialist assesses credibility and confirms whether a breach occurred.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair pass per case; missing or conflicting evidence returns to the investigator.
loop.why_not_simpler: Accounts of events and policy qualifications are narrative and cannot be resolved through threshold rules alone.

steps.what: Decide findings and proportionate corrective actions with the operations manager.
Write the investigation report and corrective action record.
Release findings and corrective actions to responsible managers.

tasks.design: A restricted case register in {WORKFLOW} accepts concerns and links uploaded evidence from {DOCS}, with optional read-only connections to {OPS_SYSTEM}, {PROCUREMENT} and {ERP}. A bounded comparison loop prepares an evidence table; people conduct inspections, interviews and findings decisions. Approved decision fields generate the report and corrective actions, with release approval and reminders through {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered and site conditions cannot be inferred reliably from records. Trust, access restrictions and disputed accounts prevent complete automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured case records and deterministic evidence retrieval can remove administrative work. Bounded text comparison can expose gaps while retaining investigator responsibility.
tasks.still_hard: Physical verification, credibility assessment, protected disclosures and legally sensitive escalation remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: The investigator notices unsafe conditions, earns cooperation and weighs conflicting testimony fairly.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on preventive controls for recurring waste-handling incidents.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling files and more time testing root causes and checking corrective actions. Authority over findings, sanctions and regulator reporting does not change.

reach.task: Prepare an evidence-based response to an environmental incident.
reach.learn: Learn incident communication, disclosure timing and how to protect confidential investigation details.

evidence.claim: Case registers, evidence links and action reminders can support environmental investigations without automating findings.
GDPR Article 22 requires assessment where automation makes decisions with significant effects on individuals.
The digest identifies Dutch works council consent rules for employee data and monitoring; national requirements elsewhere vary.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The typical case involves internal policy investigation and manager follow-up.
The starter uses restricted uploads; live integrations are optional.
The build estimate excludes surveillance, automatic misconduct scoring and regulator submission.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability require deployment-specific assessment; employee consultation follows national rules.
The low full-automation prior fits the substantial inspection and conversation time.
unknowns: Which environmental policies and reporting obligations apply.
Whether concerns include protected disclosures or employee allegations.
Which roles may access evidence and approve case findings.
Whether works council or employee consultation is required under applicable national rules.
Which records reliably identify the relevant site, waste stream and period.
research_questions: Can case evidence be retrieved without exposing unrelated employee information?
Which policy comparisons can use deterministic thresholds?
Does the evidence table improve completeness without biasing investigators toward a breach finding?
new_work: Review evidence gaps and erroneous record matches.
Maintain policy versions, access permissions and retention rules.
Check that corrective actions are completed and effective.
Arrange applicable employee consultation before changing monitoring practices.
Prepare required external notices through a separate authorized approval process.
tasks.statement: Identify or investigate violations of natural resources, waste management, recycling, or other environmental policies.

tasks.short: Define useful sustainability indicators, test their data and agree how they will guide decisions.

steps.what: Agree the sustainability outcome and decision the indicator should support.
Review existing indicators, technical definitions and reporting guidance.

loop.input: Approved definitions and guidance relevant to the indicator brief.
loop.output: Candidate indicators with source definitions, boundaries, units and stated limitations.
loop.check: Verify definition quotations; flag missing boundaries and separate source definitions from proposed adaptations.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass over at most 15 sources; unsupported candidates are excluded.
loop.why_not_simpler: Definitions and limitations appear in varied narrative passages rather than consistent fields.

steps.what: Inspect available operating data and identify suitable fields and gaps.
Specify formulas, units, organizational boundaries, exclusions and data owners.
Calculate trial values and test missing data, sensitivity and comparability.
Approve the indicator and its intended management use.
Register the approved definition and configure its reporting view.

tasks.design: An indicator register in {WORKFLOW} stores definitions, boundaries, owners and approval versions, starting with uploaded exports from {OPS_SYSTEM}, {ERP} or {PROCUREMENT}. Deterministic calculations on {DATA_PLATFORM} test coverage and sensitivity and populate {BI}; a bounded reading loop prepares sourced candidate definitions. People select meaningful measures and approve their management use before activation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The main obstacle was agreeing meaningful boundaries and obtaining comparable data. Calculations were already possible, but repeatable tests and definition management required setup work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can make small calculation services and data-quality views cheaper to build. Structured definitions let the same tests run whenever a candidate formula changes.
tasks.still_hard: Missing physical measurements, inconsistent denominators and incentives to improve the score without improving the outcome remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist chooses measures that reflect real environmental outcomes and anticipates unintended incentives.

ambition.what: Monthly site waste-prevention priorities based on comparable intensity and absolute-volume indicators.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time recalculating trial measures and more time discussing whether they support useful decisions. Management retains authority over targets and investment unless explicitly delegated.

reach.task: Write clear measurement instructions for site teams.
reach.learn: Learn procedural writing, worked examples and how to test instructions with first-time users.

evidence.claim: Versioned metric definitions, deterministic calculations and data-quality dashboards can reduce indicator development effort.
Creating a meaningful indicator still requires decisions about boundaries, comparability and behavioral incentives.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The starter covers one indicator family and existing data, without new metering equipment.
The build estimate includes approval versioning and a small trial dashboard.
Aggregate operational indicators are preferred; employee-level measures require separate GDPR, EU AI Act and national-rules assessment.
The creation-heavy prior supports retaining human indicator design while automating trial calculations.
unknowns: Which decisions the organization wants the indicators to support.
Whether quantities, units and site boundaries are consistent in existing records.
Which data owners can validate completeness and measurement methods.
Whether indicators will be used for employee evaluation or external claims.
Who may approve definition changes and historical restatements.
research_questions: Which candidate indicators change materially under reasonable boundary choices?
Can source data distinguish missing values from genuine zero activity?
Do proposed indicators lead to different operational decisions than existing measures?
new_work: Review data-quality exceptions and changes in coverage.
Maintain unit conversions, formula versions and source mappings.
Explain restatements when definitions or source data change.
Check whether indicator incentives encourage undesirable behavior.
tasks.statement: Identify or create new sustainability indicators.

tasks.short: Prepare funding applications and project proposals for sustainability initiatives.

steps.what: Read funding guidance and identify eligibility, evidence and submission requirements.

loop.input: Current funding guidance and the application template.
loop.output: A checklist of eligibility conditions, deadlines, attachments and assessment criteria with source references.
loop.check: Check every condition against a source passage; validate dates and required sections mechanically.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per guidance pack; ambiguous or conflicting conditions go to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Funding conditions and exceptions are expressed in varying prose and document layouts.

steps.what: Decide whether the project qualifies and merits an application.
Collect approved project facts, supplier quotations and supporting evidence.
Calculate eligible costs, funding requested and the project financing gap.
Draft the application narrative, outcomes, delivery plan and supporting annexes.

loop.input: Application template, reviewed funding checklist, approved project evidence and calculated funding budget.
loop.output: A draft application with traceable claims, populated annexes and explicit evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections, length limits, numerical consistency and source references; specialist reviews claims and commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per section; unsupported claims remain flagged and block finalisation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative answers must explain project relevance and outcomes against funding criteria expressed in free text.

steps.what: Resolve delivery commitments, partner contributions and outstanding evidence gaps.
Approve application declarations, financial commitments and the final submission version.
Enter application fields, upload attachments and submit the approved version.
Archive the submission and record response dates and follow-up obligations.

tasks.design: Use {WORKFLOW} to collect approved evidence from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}, and deterministic calculations to generate the funding budget from {ERP} data. Bounded reading and drafting loops produce a sourced application in {DOCS}; the authorised signatory approves its exact version before the specialist submits it through the {GOV_PORTAL}. Generate a submission pack and record the receipt and follow-up dates in {PROJECT} and {CALENDAR}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each funding call has different wording, templates and evidence requirements. Project facts and financial inputs arrive from several teams, making reusable application assembly difficult.
tasks.enabler_now: Document templates, validation rules and configured collection workflows already cover much of the work. Bounded models can extract prose requirements and draft from approved evidence; AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of assembling these components.
tasks.still_hard: Eligibility ambiguities, credible impact estimates and binding delivery commitments require judgement. Portal authentication and changing forms can keep submission partly manual.
tasks.human_edge: Choose projects worth funding, defend realistic environmental outcomes and secure commitments that delivery teams can honour.

ambition.what: Funding application support for site teams without grant-writing capacity.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more of the week testing funding fit and strengthening project evidence, with less repetitive drafting. They can support smaller site proposals; formal commitment and signature rights remain with existing approvers.

reach.task: Prepare evidence-based project descriptions and implementation annexes.
reach.learn: Structured authoring, source traceability and explaining technical outcomes to non-specialist assessors.

evidence.claim: Template assembly, funding calculations, completeness checks and deadline tracking suit deterministic technology.
Bounded drafting from approved sources can reduce application preparation, but the digest provides no sustainability-grant automation case.
The reported Deloitte case illustrates why generated references and factual claims need source validation.
Remaining-time percentages and build ranges are design estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The initial build covers one funding scheme and one application template.
Internal proposals use the same evidence and drafting components but follow internal submission routes.
Evidence collection retrieves approved records and requests missing inputs; it does not generate missing facts.
Finance approves cost eligibility rules and assumptions before automated calculations are used.
The submission pack is generated automatically; portal entry and final submission remain human work.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access and employee consultation under national rules are assessed for the actual implementation; no employee evaluation or monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Which funding schemes, applicant entities and submission portals are used?
Are approved project facts, baselines and quotations available in reusable records?
Who confirms cost eligibility, impact assumptions and financial commitments?
Which declarations require signatures, and which portal access methods are permitted?
What confidentiality restrictions, access approvals and employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: What are the current scheme rules for eligible costs, funding combinations and supporting evidence?
Does the relevant portal support imports or structured uploads?
Which environmental outcome methods does the funder accept?
new_work: Review extracted conditions and resolve ambiguous eligibility requirements.
Check narrative claims, sources and commitments before sign-off.
Maintain templates, funding rules and cost calculation versions.
Track missing evidence, failed collections and submission receipts.
Update follow-up schedules when the funder changes deadlines or requests clarification.
tasks.statement: Write grant applications, rebate applications, or project proposals to secure funding for sustainability projects.

tasks.short: Answer sustainability questions, help teams apply program requirements and coordinate administrative follow-up.

steps.what: Read incoming requests and record topic, site, urgency and responsible owner.
Find current guidance, relevant records and previous answers.
Prepare an answer, checklist or administrative instructions for the request.

loop.input: The request, approved guidance sections and a response template.
loop.output: A source-linked draft answer or checklist with explicit gaps.
loop.check: Require current source references; check scope and dates; flag commitments and missing guidance.
loop.stop: Use a fixed template for standard questions. Otherwise allow one draft and one repair, then return unresolved requests to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Standard replies need no model, but contextual questions require interpreting prose and adapting instructions.

steps.what: Discuss complex questions and adapt advice to local operating conditions.
Decide requests for exceptions, changed requirements or program commitments.
Check and send the final response to the internal requester.
Record the answer, follow-up owner and reusable guidance candidate.

tasks.design: A configured intake in {WORKFLOW} captures request categories and routes cases; a deterministic index retrieves approved guidance from {DOCS}. Templates handle standard answers, while a bounded loop drafts contextual replies for specialist review. People handle complex advice and program exceptions, then {WORKFLOW} releases approved replies through {EMAIL} or {CHAT} and records follow-up in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests arrived without consistent details, guidance was difficult to find, and answers stayed in individual conversations.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, routing, tagged guidance and response templates cover much of the work. A small drafting loop can adapt approved material to varied questions.
tasks.still_hard: Local technical conditions can invalidate a standard answer. Keeping guidance current and distinguishing advice from a program exception require accountable people.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist recognises when a question conceals an operational obstacle and helps the requester find a workable approach.

ambition.what: A scheduled sustainability advice clinic for small regional offices without local specialist support.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time searching and recording answers and more time resolving difficult local cases. They can gain authority to close routine guidance requests under an agreed service charter; program exceptions remain with the program owner.

reach.task: Turn recurring sustainability questions into tested operating instructions.
reach.learn: Task-based writing, version control and usability testing with operational readers.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, category routing, tagged retrieval and approved-message delivery can use deterministic configuration.
Contextual drafting can support specialists, but no direct sustainability support accuracy or savings case appears in the digest.

assumptions: The service initially supports internal requesters and does not send public environmental claims.
Most new requests can use structured intake; unstructured or misclassified requests retain human triage time.
Complex discussions and exception approvals occur only for relevant cases; their shares are averages across the request mix.
Review time is included in the remaining percentages; logging a guidance candidate does not publish new guidance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; access controls and retention cover personal information in requests.
Access and consultation ranges allow for national rules where applicable; local arrangements may extend elapsed delivery time.
unknowns: Request volumes, recurring topics and the proportion needing technical investigation.
Which guidance is approved, current and owned.
Current response authority and exception approval rights.
Ability to require structured intake without excluding regional staff.
Sensitive information in support history and applicable national consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which frequent questions can be answered entirely with fixed templates?
Can topic tags retrieve sufficient guidance without semantic search?
Which cases must be routed directly to technical, procurement or legal colleagues?
How will regional staff test whether the advice clinic addresses their actual needs?
new_work: Review contextual replies and handle incomplete requests.
Maintain topic tags, routing rules and approved response templates.
Approve or reject guidance candidates before publication.
Remove outdated guidance and inspect failed retrievals.
Run the regional advice clinic and track unresolved operational issues.
tasks.statement: Provide technical or administrative support for sustainability programs or issues.

tasks.short: Identify and procure resources for sustainability projects.

steps.what: Agree project requirements, environmental outcomes and resource constraints.
Check existing contracts, equipment and available internal capacity.
Request supplier quotations and supporting environmental evidence.
Compare supplier evidence against technical and environmental requirements.

loop.input: Supplier quotations and environmental evidence, checked against the resource brief.
loop.output: A sourced comparison with missing evidence and conflicting claims flagged.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source passages; specialist checks material claims and comparability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per document; unreadable or unsupported claims enter an exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents express certifications, exclusions and performance claims in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Calculate whole-life costs and compare resource options.
Negotiate delivery constraints and agree the preferred resource option.
Enter the purchase requisition and attach the selection evidence.
Approve the resource choice and spending commitment.
Issue the purchase order and record the delivery commitment.

tasks.design: Connect {PROCUREMENT}, {ERP} and {PROJECT} to identify reusable resources and generate cost comparisons from approved assumptions. A bounded document loop prepares sourced supplier assessments in {DOCS}, while configured {PROCUREMENT} workflows request quotations, assemble requisitions and issue orders only after spending approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Resource records, quotations and environmental evidence sit in separate places. Supplier claims need interpretation, and occasional projects rarely justify bespoke integration.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing purchasing workflows handle requests and approvals. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors and cost calculators; bounded extraction can handle varied documents.
tasks.still_hard: Verifying environmental claims, comparing different technical solutions and negotiating scarce resources remain demanding. Internal capacity records may be incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether a resource will deliver the intended environmental outcome under real operating conditions, and negotiate workable commitments.

ambition.what: Quarterly recommendations to reallocate uncommitted sustainability project resources.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time collecting quotations and assembling requisitions, and more time comparing interventions. They can recommend resource reallocations more often; spending authority remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Compare environmental and financial trade-offs for campaign materials and events.
reach.learn: Campaign production constraints, supplier specifications and how material choices affect campaign delivery.

evidence.claim: Resource matching, cost calculations and approval routing can use deterministic integrations and configured workflows.
Pactum inside Coupa provides evidence for requisition policy checking, not verification of sustainability claims.
Sourced document extraction can assist comparison of supplier evidence; these time estimates are unvalidated design estimates.

assumptions: The company has purchasing records, an asset register and project resource plans, although their quality varies.
Routine quotation requests use approved templates and supplier lists and create no purchasing commitment.
Cost calculations use versioned assumptions; missing material inputs block a comparison.
Build ranges cover one initial resource category and exclude supplier onboarding and contract negotiation.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access is limited to necessary business data; employee consultation under national rules is included where the implementation changes staff processes or data use.
unknowns: Which resource categories, internal capacity records and interfaces are available?
Which environmental criteria and evidence standards are approved?
Who can approve spending, supplier selection and changes to project allocations?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules are required?
research_questions: Which environmental certifications and performance methods allow valid comparison for the selected resource category?
Which existing purchasing features can cover requests, approvals and order release without custom code?
new_work: Review extracted supplier claims and resolve conflicting or missing evidence.
Maintain resource categories, cost assumptions and environmental comparison rules.
Handle failed requests, stale capacity records and integration exceptions.
Check that issued orders match the approved requisition.
tasks.statement: Identify or procure needed resources to implement sustainability programs or projects.

tasks.short: Create sustainability project plans, supporting documents, and recurring updates.

steps.what: Gather the proposal, policy requirements, evidence, and resource estimates.
Agree scope, outcomes, responsibilities, and major dependencies with project owners.
Record activities, owners, dates, costs, and dependencies in the project plan.
Prepare the business case, risk notes, and supporting project documents.

loop.input: Project plan, approved cost calculations, source evidence, and document templates.
loop.output: Business case narrative and evidence-linked risk notes.
loop.check: Reconcile costs to fixed calculations; verify assumptions and evidence; specialist checks omitted risks.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing costs or evidence block readiness for approval.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed calculations cover costs, but project-specific rationale and risk descriptions require prose interpretation.

steps.what: Approve the project scope, budget, and resource commitments.
Send routine requests for project status updates.
Copy owner updates into the plan and supporting status documents.

tasks.design: Configure templates, owner updates, and scheduled reminders in the {PROJECT}, with approval records in the {WORKFLOW}. A generator assembles evidence from the {DOCS}, uses fixed cost calculations, and adds a bounded loop for business case wording. Factual status updates refresh documents automatically; changes to scope, budget, or commitments return to human approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans, cost assumptions, and status documents were maintained separately. Project-specific reasoning resisted simple document templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing project features can remove chasing and copying. Faster code assembly makes linked documents and fixed calculations affordable, with bounded drafting for narrative sections.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies, realistic delivery dates, and resource negotiations remain human planning work. Owner updates may still be incomplete or optimistic.
tasks.human_edge: Build a deliverable plan that reflects operational constraints and secure real commitments from owners.

ambition.what: A ready-to-review green event project pack for event planners.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends more time on project choices and delivery risks, with less document maintenance. They can prepare smaller projects for sponsor review without gaining spending authority.

reach.task: Plan event waste prevention, venue requirements, and supplier responsibilities.
reach.learn: Event delivery timelines, venue constraints, supplier lead times, and attendee needs.

evidence.claim: Project templates, structured owner updates, and reminders can replace routine plan administration.
Business case narrative can be drafted from approved inputs while calculations and commitment approvals remain separate.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The document-generation prior understates the human effort needed to negotiate and structure a viable plan.
The {PROJECT} supports templates, structured status updates, and reminders.
Project owners enter factual updates directly; scope and budget changes do not take effect automatically.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and may overlap.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Named owner records are limited to delivery needs; national rules may require consultation if reporting becomes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which project features are already licensed and enabled?
Who approves budgets, dependencies, and revised delivery commitments?
Will project owners maintain structured status records?
Which documents must be retained separately for finance or assurance?
What employee consultation is required under national rules?
research_questions: Which supporting documents can become generated views of the project record?
Can the existing {PROJECT} distinguish factual updates from approval-requiring changes?
new_work: Review business case drafts and project-specific risk omissions.
Maintain templates, cost assumptions, and document mappings.
Escalate late or contradictory owner updates.
Train project owners to enter updates and raise change requests.
Monitor reminders, access permissions, and approval routing.
tasks.statement: Create or maintain plans or other documents related to sustainability projects.

tasks.short: Prepare reports and presentations explaining sustainability initiative results.

steps.what: Export initiative spending and savings from the finance records.
Export resource use, waste quantities, and operational activity.
Reconcile periods, units, baselines, and missing figures in the reporting workbook.
Build charts and tables in the report or presentation template.
Write the interpretation, limitations, and recommended actions.

loop.input: Validated metrics, baseline definitions, project decisions, and approved supporting evidence.
loop.output: Narrative explaining measured changes, limitations, and proposed actions.
loop.check: Match every number to validated metrics and every factual claim to a source; specialist checks causality.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported explanations become explicit unknowns.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates can state metric changes, but contextual explanations require reading project evidence.

steps.what: Review conclusions and approve the report for its intended audience.
Publish the approved report for internal readers.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations bring {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} records into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, where fixed rules calculate metrics and expose exceptions in the {BI}. A deterministic generator builds figures in the {DOCS}, and a bounded loop drafts explanations from validated evidence. The {WORKFLOW} records approval before internal publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finance and operational records used different periods, identifiers, and units. Reports required repeated copying and formatting.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors, explicit metric definitions, and cheaper template generation make the routine pipeline practical. A small drafting loop can explain the validated results.
tasks.still_hard: Poor baselines, missing supplier data, and attributing improvements to a particular initiative remain difficult. External claims require audience-specific review.
tasks.human_edge: Explain what the figures justify, challenge weak causal claims, and recommend action despite uncertainty.

ambition.what: Monthly intervention decisions for sustainability initiatives missing their targets.

tasks.altitude: Routine report assembly gives way to investigating exceptions and discussing corrective action. The specialist gains authority to recommend intervention priorities, while sponsors retain budget decisions.

reach.task: Prepare evidence-backed explanations of sustainability results for external audiences.
reach.learn: Claim substantiation, audience context, and review requirements for environmental communications.

evidence.claim: Structured reporting data supports deterministic calculations, charts, and document generation.
The digest documents a government report containing nonexistent sources, supporting explicit citation checks.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are estimates for recurring internal reporting.
Operational records are available in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; supplier documents may require a different connector.
The reporting prior fits: most savings come from deterministic assembly, with a small narrative loop.
Metric definitions and baseline changes require explicit approval.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and may overlap.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Access uses aggregated data where possible; national consultation rules apply if employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Where are resource use, waste, and building performance records actually held?
Are initiative identifiers shared between financial and operational records?
Which baselines, conversion factors, and reporting boundaries have been approved?
Which reports are public, statutory, or subject to assurance?
Does any source reveal individual employee activity?
research_questions: Can a historical report be reproduced from source records with matching totals and provenance?
Can existing {BI} and {DOCS} features generate the required report formats?
new_work: Review unit, period, completeness, and baseline exceptions.
Maintain metric definitions, source mappings, and report templates.
Check narrative claims and distinguish correlation from causation.
Monitor failed refreshes and reconcile corrected source records.
tasks.statement: Develop reports or presentations to communicate the effectiveness of sustainability initiatives.

tasks.short: Create and publish sustainability communication materials supported by approved evidence.

steps.what: Agree the audience, purpose, format and intended response.
Select approved facts, procedures, images and supporting evidence.
Write copy that explains the sustainability issue and requested action.

loop.input: Content brief, approved claim evidence and channel constraints.
loop.output: Copy draft with claim references and preserved qualifications.
loop.check: Compare numbers with approved values; require references for environmental claims and human review of implied claims.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision, capped at two model calls; unsupported claims are removed or returned for evidence.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanations require varied prose; fixed templates handle only routine notices.

steps.what: Lay out the brochure or prepare the website page using approved assets.
Check factual claims, qualifications, readability and evidence in the publication proof.
Approve the exact proof, channel and publication date.
Publish the approved page or distribute the approved brochure.

tasks.design: An approved claim and asset register in {DOCS} feeds a bounded copy loop and deterministic brochure or page templates. {WORKFLOW} records approval for the exact publication version and permits release through {CMS} or {MARKETING_AUTOMATION} only while that approval remains valid. A file-based starter produces reviewable proofs before publication access is available.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence, copy and layout were handled separately, making revisions slow and approvals hard to trace. Templates existed, but reusable claim records and publication connections needed implementation.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can accelerate template generation and approval connections. A bounded writing loop can adapt approved evidence to an audience while deterministic checks preserve numbers and version control.
tasks.still_hard: Implied environmental claims, persuasive framing, original visual concepts and unfamiliar audiences still require expert review.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist judges whether the overall message is fair, understandable and supported, including what readers may infer.

ambition.what: Provide plain-language waste-sorting guides for temporary site staff.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repetitive drafting and layout coordination toward audience testing and evidence review. Publication authority stays with the marketing manager.

reach.task: Edit sustainability material for clarity and defensible claims.
reach.learn: Learn copy editing, source checking and how to preserve qualifications during shortening.

reach.task: Design clear waste-sorting instructions for site use.
reach.learn: Learn visual hierarchy, accessible contrast and testing whether symbols are understood.

evidence.claim: Shopify Sidekick demonstrates commercial copy drafting; this evidence does not establish sustainability claim accuracy.
Approved templates can generate routine publication layouts and preserve source-linked values.
The documented report with nonexistent references supports validating generated factual claims before release.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The estimate covers two approved templates and an existing asset library.
Routine layout becomes automatic; original campaign design is outside this estimate.
Publication approval time is counted in s6; s7 enforces that approval without a second review.
Any change to the approved proof invalidates publication approval.
The high automation prior is moderated by environmental claim review and audience judgment.
GDPR and EU AI Act applicability are assessed for the deployment; consultation and employment requirements follow national rules.
unknowns: Which claims have current evidence and permission for public use.
Who approves environmental claims and when legal review is required.
Which publication channels allow configured approval and version controls.
Whether temporary staff need translated or accessible formats.
Whether mailing lists, photographs or other assets contain personal data.
research_questions: Can all factual claims be linked to current approved evidence?
Do intended readers understand the requested action after viewing the proof?
Do template checks catch clipped text, missing qualifications and inaccessible layouts?
Can the publication connection guarantee that only the approved version is released?
new_work: Maintain claim evidence, expiry dates and asset permissions.
Review generated copy and the overall implied message.
Inspect rendered proofs and test instructions with intended readers.
Maintain templates and publication connections.
Withdraw or update materials when supporting evidence changes.
tasks.statement: Create marketing or outreach media, such as brochures or Web sites, to communicate sustainability issues, procedures, or objectives.

tasks.short: Gather and assess waste management and green building evidence for decision makers.

steps.what: Clarify the decision, site constraints, and evidence needed.
Retrieve local waste, resource use, and building performance records.
Search public research websites for waste and building evidence.
Read publications and record findings, qualifications, dates, and sources.

loop.input: Retrieved publications and a fixed evidence schema tied to the research question.
loop.output: Findings with exact passages, dates, geography, methods, and limitations.
loop.check: Verify passages against stored sources; require units and context; specialist checks relevant and conflicting findings.
loop.stop: At most 20 documents and one retry per document; unreadable or insufficient sources go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Publications express findings and caveats in varied prose that fixed field extraction misses.

steps.what: Compare options against local costs, constraints, and evidence quality.
Check practical assumptions with facilities staff during a site walk.
Prepare a cited decision brief with options and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Reviewed option assessment, site notes, and cited evidence.
loop.output: Decision brief separating findings, assumptions, options, and unanswered questions.
loop.check: Verify citations and numerical consistency; specialist approves the brief before release to decision makers.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported statements are removed or marked unknown.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template supplies headings but cannot concisely explain conflicting evidence and site qualifications.

tasks.design: A source collector on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieves approved public research websites through the {OTHER} and joins local exports from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. A bounded extraction loop builds a cited evidence register in the {DOCS}, while deterministic tables support option comparison. The specialist checks site applicability and releases a reviewed decision brief; investment decisions remain separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research sources were dispersed and difficult to compare. Findings lacked consistent units, dates, local context, and traceable qualifications.
tasks.enabler_now: Cheaper source connectors and evidence records reduce repetitive searching. Bounded extraction can turn prose into reviewable findings without autonomous browsing.
tasks.still_hard: Source coverage, inaccessible publications, promotional claims, and transferability to a particular building remain expensive to assess. Physical conditions still need local verification.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether evidence applies to the site and identify practical constraints that publications omit.

ambition.what: Evidence briefs for small office sites that previously received little specialist support.

tasks.altitude: The specialist answers more site questions and spends more time testing applicability. They gain responsibility for evidence triage and recommending local trials, without gaining investment approval rights.

reach.role: Market Research Analysts and Marketing Specialists
reach.task: Compare environmental attributes and evidence quality across market offerings.
reach.learn: Research sampling, source bias, comparable product boundaries, and separating supplier claims from verified findings.

evidence.claim: Approved-source retrieval and structured evidence records can reduce repetitive research preparation.
Evidence extraction from prose benefits from bounded model use, while local applicability requires specialist judgement.

assumptions: Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The gathering-heavy prior fits, but collecting information does not eliminate applicability checks or site conversations.
The first version searches an approved source list with defined queries; broader discovery remains an exception.
Local records are available through the {OPS_SYSTEM}; actual storage may differ.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot and may overlap.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Employee-level records are unnecessary for the initial design; national consultation rules apply if that changes.
unknowns: Which buildings, waste streams, and decisions are in scope?
Are local measurements complete and comparable across periods?
Which publications can be retrieved and stored under existing access rights?
How much evidence requires supplier contact or physical inspection?
Who can approve a trial or investment after receiving the brief?
research_questions: Does the approved source list cover the most common site questions adequately?
Can extraction preserve caveats, geography, dates, and units on a representative document set?
Which recurring questions can use fixed comparison tables without a model?
new_work: Review extracted findings and conflicting evidence.
Maintain source lists, retrieval permissions, and freshness rules.
Handle unavailable publications and gaps in local measurements.
Validate site assumptions and record why evidence was accepted or rejected.
Maintain extraction schemas and monitor retrieval costs.
tasks.statement: Collect information about waste stream management or green building practices to inform decision makers.

tasks.short: Assess sustainability initiatives for cost, feasibility and acceptance, then recommend which to pursue.

steps.what: Read initiative submissions and supporting documents to establish the proposal and evidence gaps.

loop.input: Submitted proposals, approved baseline data and an evidence checklist.
loop.output: A source-linked brief distinguishing stated facts, supplier claims and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require page references; verify extracted costs and quantities against sources; reject unsupported fields.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair; maximum two calls per submission. Unreadable or conflicting evidence returns to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier proposals use varied prose and layouts; fixed fields cannot reliably capture qualifications and exclusions.

steps.what: Inspect the affected site or process with operational colleagues.
Calculate investment costs, operating savings and environmental scenarios.
Test technical feasibility, delivery constraints and likely acceptance with affected teams.
Weigh alternatives and select a recommendation, including uncertainty and trade-offs.
Write the business case and proposed implementation conditions.

loop.input: The specialist's recommendation, validated calculations, feasibility findings and business-case template.
loop.output: A business case with sourced claims, risks and proposed implementation conditions.
loop.check: Match all numbers to calculated scenarios; retain uncertainty and objections; require specialist review.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; maximum two calls per case. Unsupported passages remain flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be templated, but the rationale must connect varied technical findings and acceptance concerns.

steps.what: Approve, reject or request a pilot within the applicable investment authority.
Record the decision, conditions and next review date.

tasks.design: A structured intake in {WORKFLOW} links proposal evidence in {DOCS} to a deterministic scenario calculator on {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded loops extract qualified claims and draft the business case using the specialist's chosen recommendation. People assess feasibility and acceptance, the budget owner approves commitments, and {PROJECT} records the decision and review conditions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proposals were hard to compare, calculations were rebuilt for each case, and supplier claims required careful reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable calculation modules and evidence templates reduce repeated analysis. Bounded extraction and drafting can handle varied documents without delegating investment decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Actual performance, technical suitability and staff acceptance may only become clear through a pilot. Environmental benefits can depend heavily on boundaries and assumptions.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist challenges attractive but weak claims and weighs practical acceptance against cost and environmental benefit.

ambition.what: A small-project sustainability appraisal clinic for departmental proposals.

tasks.altitude: The specialist can appraise smaller proposals that previously lacked analytical support and spend more time designing useful pilots. They can gain authority to recommend pilot conditions; investment approval remains with the budget owner.

reach.task: Assess the commercial value and claim implications of a proposed sustainability initiative.
reach.learn: Customer research, commercial scenario design and substantiation of environmental claims.

evidence.claim: Cost scenarios and sensitivity calculations are deterministic once assumptions and methods are approved.
Bounded document extraction and drafting are plausible support tools; the digest contains no direct sustainability appraisal performance case.

assumptions: The initial scope covers recurring initiative types with agreed calculation methods.
Site visits and investment decisions remain human work.
Supplier claims remain labelled as claims until independently supported.
Time shares represent an appraisal mix; not every initiative requires an equally long site visit.
Build ranges assume reusable templates and accessible source files; they do not assume a scientific breakthrough.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. Changes affecting staff may require consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Investment thresholds and pilot approval rights.
Initiative types, available baseline evidence and accepted environmental calculation methods.
Availability of technical expertise and independent supplier evidence.
Which proposals change working conditions and which national consultation arrangements apply.
Actual volume of smaller proposals currently left unassessed.
research_questions: Which past decisions would have changed under realistic sensitivity analysis?
Which supplier claims need independent verification before a pilot?
Can existing investment templates and calculations be configured before building a separate tool?
new_work: Verify extracted qualifications, exclusions and supplier claims.
Maintain calculation methods and cost assumptions.
Track pilot conditions and compare realised results with business cases.
Staff the additional appraisal clinic and manage its intake.
tasks.statement: Assess or propose sustainability initiatives, considering factors such as cost effectiveness, technical feasibility, and acceptance.

tasks.short: Collect, reconcile and review energy, resource, waste and recycling indicators.

steps.what: Export utility costs and waste charges from the {ERP}.
Request meter readings and waste weights from site contacts.
Compile site readings and waste records, then return a site log.
Combine site logs and expense exports in an indicator workbook.
Apply unit conversions, reporting boundaries and intensity calculations.
Review completeness, unusual movements and reconciliation differences before accepting the dataset.
Discuss deviations and agree investigations or corrective actions.
Refresh the internal dashboard with validated indicators.

tasks.design: Scheduled imports on {DATA_PLATFORM} combine expense exports from {ERP} with structured site logs collected through {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic rules calculate indicators, retain source lineage and flag gaps or unusual changes; accepted datasets feed {BI}. The specialist investigates exceptions with facilities colleagues and tracks corrective actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site identifiers, units and reporting periods differed, while manual collection tied accounting records to physical measurements.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured collection forms, scheduled imports and versioned calculation rules are established technology that can now be assembled more cheaply.
tasks.still_hard: Missing readings, shared meters, changing site boundaries and inconsistent waste measurements still require investigation. Expense totals do not establish physical consumption.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist distinguishes a real operational change from a measurement error and secures a useful response from site teams.

ambition.what: Weekly energy and waste exception triage for sites with sufficiently frequent readings.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying totals to investigating material deviations and following corrective actions. The specialist can gain authority to open investigations within agreed thresholds; operational spending rights do not change.

reach.task: Design a defensible internal comparison of sustainability performance across sites.
reach.learn: Normalisation, missing-data treatment and how to communicate uncertainty in comparisons.

evidence.claim: Structured imports, unit conversions, completeness tests and dashboard refreshes can run deterministically.
The digest's general records-and-monitoring pattern supports this architecture, but provides no direct sustainability monitoring case.

assumptions: Site logs contain structured quantities; arbitrary invoice extraction is outside the initial build.
Manual meter reading and obtaining missing waste records remain in the site contact's time.
Time shares cover the end-to-end task, including site contacts, and are estimates rather than measured savings.
The structured-data prior supports a deterministic design; the mailbox coordinates collection rather than holding most analytical work.
The build covers internal operational monitoring, not statutory reporting or external assurance.
Site-level aggregation is the default. GDPR, the EU AI Act and national rules must be assessed if employee-level monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Which sites have automatic meters, usable exports or manual readings.
Completeness of physical quantities and reporting periods.
Agreed site boundaries, indicator definitions and activity denominators.
Whether data can identify employees and which employee consultation arrangements apply.
Existing dashboard capabilities, permissions and refresh limits.
research_questions: Which indicators can support weekly decisions without implying unavailable measurement frequency?
Which reconciliations detect actual errors rather than ordinary billing timing differences?
Can collection use existing forms and dashboard configuration before custom code is needed?
new_work: Resolve validation exceptions and missing submissions.
Maintain site mappings, unit conversions and indicator definitions.
Monitor failed imports and late source corrections.
Review additional weekly alerts and remove thresholds that generate noise.
tasks.statement: Monitor or track sustainability indicators, such as energy usage, natural resource usage, waste generation, and recycling.

tasks.short: Develop sustainability goals and strategies with colleagues and secure agreement on priorities.

steps.what: Collect approved performance reports, commitments and existing plans.
Discuss priorities, dependencies and proposed goals with operational colleagues.
Calculate target trajectories, resource needs and delivery scenarios.
Write goals, measures, milestones and responsibilities into a strategy proposal.

loop.input: Agreed goals, calculated scenarios, source references and an approved strategy template.
loop.output: A strategy proposal with source references and explicit unresolved choices.
loop.check: Check numbers against scenario outputs, require sources for claims, and flag unagreed commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair; maximum two calls per proposal. Unresolved sections return to the specialist.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates assemble measures, but explaining trade-offs requires writing from varied meeting notes.

steps.what: Agree targets, funding boundaries and accountable owners.
Enter approved initiatives, owners and milestones into the delivery plan.

tasks.design: An integration assembles approved evidence from {BI}, {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; a deterministic scenario calculator on {DATA_PLATFORM} produces comparable target paths. A bounded drafting loop prepares the proposal in {DOCS}, while people negotiate priorities and approve commitments. A configured {WORKFLOW} transfers approved milestones and owners into {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, scenario workbooks differed, and negotiated choices were difficult to separate from document production.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors, calculation libraries and document templates make a small planning tool practical. Bounded drafting can turn agreed inputs into readable proposals.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing credible targets, securing operational ownership and resolving competing investment needs remain difficult. Faster drafting does not improve weak baseline evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist connects environmental consequences to business choices and earns agreement from people who must deliver them.

ambition.what: Quarterly reprioritisation of the sustainability investment portfolio.

tasks.altitude: The specialist spends less time assembling proposals and more time testing target choices with operational leaders. They can gain authority to convene quarterly portfolio reviews; funding approval remains with the executive sponsor.

reach.task: Translate approved sustainability priorities into campaign planning.
reach.learn: Campaign planning, audience needs and the evidence required for public environmental claims.

evidence.claim: Evidence assembly, scenario calculations and milestone transfer are suitable for deterministic implementation; this design is an estimate.
The digest documents a government report containing nonexistent sources, supporting explicit source checks for generated proposals.

assumptions: The baseline represents a mid-size European company with a small sustainability team and shared operational ownership.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors, not measured savings.
Approved baselines and cost assumptions exist; the tool does not invent environmental factors or commitments.
Build ranges cover one planning process and a small source set, not enterprise data remediation.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the actual deployment.
unknowns: Current strategy approval rights and spending limits.
Location, quality and ownership of approved baseline data.
Existing connector access and document permissions.
Whether employee information enters planning documents and which national consultation arrangements apply.
research_questions: Which scenario calculations recur often enough to standardise?
Can existing permissions restrict the evidence pack to approved, current sources?
Which proposed goals have failed because of operational acceptance rather than missing analysis?
new_work: Review generated proposals and unresolved source references.
Maintain scenario assumptions and document templates.
Repair source connections and reconcile changed target definitions.
Facilitate the additional quarterly portfolio review.
tasks.statement: Develop sustainability project goals, objectives, initiatives, or strategies in collaboration with other sustainability professionals.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward evaluating evidence, testing practical changes and negotiating credible commitments. With an explicit mandate, the specialist can convene portfolio reviews, initiate threshold-based investigations and close routine advice cases; budget and program exceptions retain their named approvers.
reach: Marketing manager: connect verified operational improvements to campaign choices and defensible environmental claims.
Market research analyst: design fair site comparisons and communicate uncertainty.
Technical writer: turn recurring support needs into clear, tested operating guidance.
skills_to_grow: Data definitions, source lineage and reconciliation.
Scenario modelling and sensitivity analysis.
Technical appraisal and pilot design.
Facilitation and operational change.
Source verification and bounded model-output review.
Environmental claim substantiation.
Privacy-aware service and workflow design.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a sustainability decision service: reliable operational indicators, quarterly portfolio reviews, appraisal support for small departmental projects and practical advice for regional offices. Expand only where evidence quality and human review capacity support it.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from gathering, copying, and formatting toward evidence assessment, site conversations, and corrective-action recommendations. The specialist gains wider advisory coverage; policy commitments, budgets, and external publication remain with their authorized approvers.
reach: Help technical writers turn sustainability policy into usable operating instructions.
Support public relations specialists with traceable evidence for sustainability communications.
Give event planners practical sustainability project packs.
Support market research analysts with comparable environmental evidence.
skills_to_grow: Metric definitions, baseline quality, and source provenance.
Evaluating research quality and local applicability.
Project economics, operational dependencies, and stakeholder negotiation.
Reviewing bounded model outputs and maintaining deterministic rules.
Writing qualified environmental claims for different audiences.
Data access, GDPR, EU AI Act applicability, and consultation under national rules.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Provide a lightweight sustainability decision service across sites: reusable evidence briefs, delivery-ready project packs, and monthly intervention recommendations, with traceable human approval of commitments.

role_batches.altitude: The specialist spends more time on site evidence, meaningful measures and credible communication, with less time collecting records and assembling documents. Authority over legal interpretations, findings, investment and public claims remains explicitly assigned to responsible roles.
reach: Support market research analysts with evidence about sustainable purchasing demand.
Support public relations specialists with verified incident facts.
Support technical writers with precise measurement and site instructions.
Support editors and graphic designers with source-linked sustainability content.
skills_to_grow: Source evaluation and legal applicability triage.
Metric design, measurement boundaries and data-quality testing.
Investigation interviewing and root-cause analysis.
Environmental claim substantiation and audience testing.
Configuring records, approval flows and deterministic calculation checks.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Offer a recurring sustainability decision clinic that combines source changes, site evidence and indicator trials into concrete operational proposals. Begin with approved uploads and reusable templates; add company integrations and delegated decision rights only when access and responsibilities are established.

role_batches.altitude: The role shifts toward selecting credible interventions, securing delivery commitments and helping more teams build fundable projects. Purchasing and funding commitments retain their existing approval rights.
reach: Help marketing managers assess environmental trade-offs in campaign procurement.
Support technical writers with traceable project evidence and outcome descriptions.
skills_to_grow: Environmental evidence assessment and whole-life costing.
Funding eligibility and project finance.
Structured evidence management and source verification.
Workflow configuration and exception handling.
Negotiating credible delivery commitments.
role_batches.ambitious_version: Run a reusable sustainability project support service that helps site teams compare resource options and prepare credible funding applications.
